question.text: Ganga Infra Trust, a Cat II AIF, has just raised INR 450 crore at first close and is about to make its maiden investment in a toll-road SPV. The IM's compliance officer asks whether a SEBI-registered custodian must be appointed before the first investment. What is the correct position under SEBI (AIF) Amendment Regulations, 2024 (effective 5-Jan-2024)?

answer.text: Custodian is mandatory only if corpus exceeds INR 500 crore — with INR 450 cr the fund is exempt
Custodian is optional for Cat II AIFs; only Cat III AIFs need a custodian compulsorily

Sponsor/Manager shall COMPULSORILY appoint a SEBI-registered custodian for safekeeping of securities, and the custodian must be appointed PRIOR to the date of first investment — corpus size is irrelevant post-2024 amendment
Custodian is required only if the AIF invests in physical commodity derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (AIF) Amendment Regulations, 2024 (w.e.f. 5-Jan-2024) made custodian appointment COMPULSORY for ALL AIFs (Cat I, II and III) — the earlier INR 500 crore threshold for Cat I/II was removed. Further, per SEBI Circular dated 12-Jan-2024, the custodian must be appointed PRIOR to the date of first investment of the scheme. The chapter explicitly states 'Sponsor or Manager of AIFs shall compulsorily appoint a custodian for safekeeping of securities of the fund.' The Trap: The INR 500 cr threshold distractor cites the OLD pre-2024 rule — a classic dated-regulation trap. The Cat III-only option is wrong on both counts (custodian is mandatory for ALL AIFs). The commodity-derivatives-only option relates to the physical settlement sub-rule, not the core custody requirement. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers this across all categories. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests it from LP due-diligence angle. Pre-2024 XIX-C papers may still cite the 500 cr threshold — ignore that; use the amended rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: For new fund launches, line up custodian onboarding BEFORE PPM filing — custodial agreement, demat accounts, and settlement SLAs take 6-8 weeks. If you miss appointment before first investment, SEBI treats it as a regulatory breach — potential inspection trigger.
